reconcile.note: Henry reads the Galilee summons and the later Jerusalem command as two sequential appointments, not a single contradictory instruction.

discrepancy.note: Strauss presses the flat command clash: Jesus cannot have sent the disciples to Galilee while also ordering them to stay in Jerusalem.

quotes.text: Here two questions inevitably arise: 1st, how can Jesus have directed the disciples to journey into Galilee, and yet at the same time have commanded them to remain in Jerusalem until Pentecost?
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), §138, on Mark 16:7 and Acts 1:4.

sides.snippet: He goes before you into Galilee. There you will see him, as he said to you.
sides.verseText: But go, tell his disciples and Peter, 'He goes before you into Galilee. There you will see him, as he said to you.'\"

sides.snippet: Don't depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father, which you heard from me.
sides.verseText: Being assembled together with them, he charged them, \"Don't depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father, which you heard from me.
